mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He (أرأيت الذي): whoever lightened the hamza made it between the hamza and the alif; and it was said: he substituted an alif for it. That is permissible even though a quiescent letter follows it, because a quiescent letter and a doubled letter may come after the alif according to the position of all the grammarians; and a quiescent letter that is not doubled may come after it according to the position of Yūnus, Abū ʿAmr and the Kufans, while Sībawayh and al-Mubarrad prohibited it. Eliding the hamza is permissible, and al-Kisāʾī read it so. (أرأيت) may be from seeing with the heart [i.e. knowing], with the second object omitted — there is remoteness in this in terms of the i'rab and the omission, though it is more fitting in meaning than seeing with the eye; or it may be from seeing with the eye, so there is no need for an omission.
